items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline. Chars voices funny cartoon characters, short and punchy.
lines: Earth once had six kinds of humans... at the same time.
Not apes. Humans. Six different branches of us.
Today, only one is left. So what happened to the other five?
Rewind about a hundred thousand years.
Europe: the Neanderthals, short and stocky.
Siberia and East Asia: the Denisovans. For years, all we had of them was a finger bone and a few teeth.
[offended, squeaky little finger bone, indignant] Hey! I'm more than a pinkie!
Java, Indonesia: the last Homo erectus, a species that lasted nearly two million years.
The island of Flores: Homo floresiensis, about one metre tall. Scientists call them... the Hobbits.
[proud, tiny, cheeky, with a dramatic pause] We prefer... fun-sized.
And the Philippines: Homo loo-zo-NEN-sis, only discovered in twenty nineteen.
Six kinds of humans, one planet. So why is there only one now?
By about forty thousand years ago, the Neanderthals were gone. One by one, the others vanished too.
Why? Scientists are still arguing... in very long papers.
But here's the twist. They didn't vanish completely.
When our ancestors met them... they had babies.
If your family comes from Europe or Asia, about one to two percent of your DNA is Neanderthal.
In Papua New Guinea, it's up to about five percent Denisovan.
[deep, smug, slow, deadpan cave-man wink] So technically... we never left.
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
